description: One row per quote issued or drafted. Versioned, because a renegotiated quote is a new version rather than an edit — you need to be able to say what the customer was actually sent.

columns.name: quote_number
columns.note: What the customer sees, e.g. Q-2026-0042

columns.name: version
columns.note: Increments on every reissue. Never edit a sent quote in place.

columns.name: supersedes
columns.note: QUOTE- id this replaces

columns.name: opportunity_id
columns.note: OPP- id. A quote should almost always belong to a deal.

columns.name: valid_until
columns.note: DERIVED from issue date plus the org's validity period. An open-ended quote is a discount with no expiry.

columns.name: currency
columns.note: ISO code this quote is denominated in. What the customer sees and agrees to. converted_total exists for reporting only and is never shown on the document.

columns.name: converted_currency
columns.note: DERIVED. Which currency converted_* is expressed in — the folder's base_currency at the moment of conversion. Stored per row rather than read from config, so a folder that later changes its base currency cannot silently reinterpret numbers already written.

columns.name: fx_rate
columns.note: DERIVED. The multiplier actually applied: amount x fx_rate = converted amount. Stored so the converted figure can be reconstructed and audited without guessing which rate was in force. 1 when the record is already in the base currency.

columns.name: fx_rate_date
columns.note: DERIVED. effective_from of the fx-rates row used. Not the same as when the conversion ran: a rate dated before the record's own date is the normal case, and a rate dated after it means no rate that old exists and fx.py --check will say so.

columns.name: fx_frozen
columns.note: DERIVED. yes once this record reaches a closed state, after which the converted figure is never recomputed — a closed number that moves with the exchange rate makes last quarter's attainment a different number every time it is read. Open records reconvert at the current rate on every run.

columns.name: subtotal_list
columns.note: DERIVED: sum of lines at list

columns.name: discount_amount
columns.note: DERIVED

columns.name: discount_pct
columns.note: DERIVED: blended across the whole quote

columns.name: subtotal
columns.note: DERIVED: after discount

columns.name: total
columns.note: DERIVED. What the customer pays.

columns.name: converted_total
columns.note: DERIVED. What the customer pays in the base currency, from total x fx_rate. Blank — never zero — when total is blank, when currency is blank, or when no rate exists for that currency. A missing conversion that reads as zero silently shrinks a forecast.

columns.name: annualised_value
columns.note: DERIVED: total over term, for multi-year comparability

columns.name: needs_approval
columns.note: DERIVED: any line past its max_discount_no_approval, or blended discount past the org threshold

columns.name: updated_opportunity
columns.note: Whether the opportunity amount was updated from this quote

columns.name: document_path
columns.note: The generated quote document

fx.note: Frozen the moment the quote leaves the building, matching the rule that a sent quote is never edited in place but reissued as a new version. Only the total converts. The line items, subtotal and discounts stay in the quote's own currency because they are what the customer agreed to, and a converted discount percentage is a number nobody quoted.
